Prince Gong Mansion is one of the most remarkable historic residences in Beijing, with a colorful past that reflects both grandeur and scandal. Originally built during the Qing Dynasty, it first belonged to Heshen, the infamous and notoriously corrupt minister who served under Emperor Qianlong. After Heshen’s downfall and confiscation of his vast wealth, the estate was granted to Prince Gong (Prince Kong), giving the mansion its present name. The complex is vast, featuring elegant courtyards, exquisite halls, and beautifully landscaped gardens. Walking through the residence, you can sense the extravagant lifestyle of its original owner—lavish details and grand architecture designed to impress. The garden is especially notable, with rockeries, pavilions, and quiet corners that contrast with the bustle of modern Beijing outside the gates
It is easy way to visit Prince Gong's Mansion, an well-known historical character. Just go to Beihai North line 6, location is about 500m away

It was very well remodeled, a lot of displays, and bathrooms were clean. But I wish they preserved more rooms in their original setups instead of turning them into either museum or shops. And, I wish they can turn off the loud speakers kept repeating asking people to exit through the back door.

The most disappointing part is the commercialisation of these heritage buildings, which has an irreversible impact to the heritage value. The surrounding around the mansion is even worse than a raw food market. If one comes in the afternoon, one may enjoy a bit peace & quite. BTW, one must book the tickets in advance to avoid the disappointment at the ticketing office.

Beijing hides such a "living history book" - Prince Gong's Mansion. From Heshen's luxurious private residence to Prince Gong Yixin's power center, from the legend of the blessing stele to the secret of the 99 and a half treasure houses, every brick and tile tells the rise and fall of the Qing Dynasty.

Beautiful well-kept mansion that was once built by the infamous corrupt politician Heshen before being repurposed as the property for imperial princes (historical enthusiast will know all the details) and it’s lucky that so many details remain or have been preserved to show the state of their past glory. A quick walk from the nearby train station, I came on a Saturday in late April so it was extremely crowded. There’s a small museum right after the entrance telling the story of the mansion and notable artefacts of its past inhabits, but a very crowded browse. Not much open inside (other than gift shops), mostly just admiring the structure from the outside. There is a wish-making wall where for around 25 yuan you can buy a tablet and write your own wish too, that comes along with a little gold good luck charm. Garden was beautiful, though hard to feel the tranquility among all the crowds. This place is close to other key attractions, just an hour is enough to see everything here. I purchased a ticket in advance but looked like tickets could be bought onsite too. Highly recommend if you want to tick off seeing the many key sights of Beijing

Prince Gong Mansion is a hidden gem in Beijing that offers a rich glimpse into Qing Dynasty history. Once the lavish home of a powerful prince, the mansion features beautifully preserved architecture, elegant gardens, and intricate cultural details that history lovers will truly appreciate. Unlike the often-crowded Forbidden City, this site is much more peaceful, making it easier to explore at your own pace and absorb the atmosphere. Be sure to leave time to stroll through the surrounding hutong neighborhood. The narrow alleyways and traditional courtyard homes offer a unique contrast to Beijing’s modern skyline and give you a deeper sense of the city’s layered past and present. Whether you’re a history buff or just looking for a quieter cultural experience, Prince Gong Mansion is well worth a visit. .

Prince Gong’s Mansion is a must-visit gem in Beijing! The historic residence is beautifully preserved and offers a fascinating glimpse into Qing dynasty life. The gardens are absolutely stunning – peaceful pathways, rockeries, and traditional pavilions that make you feel like you’ve stepped back in time. It’s a wonderful balance of culture, history, and natural beauty. Compared to some of the more crowded attractions, it feels calm and serene, perfect for a relaxing stroll while learning about Beijing’s rich heritage. Highly recommended for history lovers and anyone who enjoys traditional Chinese gardens!

During our trip to Beijing, we took the city bus from the hotel where we stayed and came to this Beijing Prince Gong’s Mansion (恭王府), a historic ancient building complex worthy of our visit and keep in our memory. Speaking of Prince Gong’s Mansion, we have to look back at the last dynasty in the long history of ancient China, that is, the Manchurian (Qing) Dynasty (1636 AD - 1912 AD), which also had a period of prosperity, and then declined under the rampant corruption of officials. Prince Gong's Mansion used to be the official mansion of The Prince Gong， after the leaving of He-Shen 和珅, the confidantes of Emperor Qianlong 乾隆 (1735 AD - 1795 AD), after his father the Emperor Yongcheng 雍正 (1722 AD - 1735 AD). Qianlong 乾隆 is one of the three wise and brilliant emperors among all emperors in the earliest decades along Manchurian (Qing 清) dynasty reign, who dare not reigned in throne longer than and overpassed the reign period of his grand father, the former emperor Kang Xi (康熙/ 1661 AD - 1722 AD), as an act of respect in that ancient society of the Manchurian dynasty. According to relevant historical documents, He-Shen (和珅), was a minister of Emperor Qianlong (乾隆) in the Manchurian (Qing 清) Dynasty who was comparable to a prime minister that trusted by the Emperor QianLong (乾隆), had great influence on Emperor Qianlong's (乾隆) ruling decisions during his tenure. He was popular with his subordinates and local officials at that time. Admired flattery and flattery, enjoyed all the bribes and offerings they provided, corrupted to the extreme, and rich in all directions of nation. It wasn't until the Chinese Nationalist Government came under the rule of the Communist government that it completely overthrew the dynastic system and took the line of democracy and communism. After taking over Prince Gong's Mansion into nationalized control, it was discovered and confiscated some of He-Shen's (和珅) and Prince Gong's （恭亲王）legacy of jewelry and antiques. There are many traces of loss of belongings, jewelry and antiques, during the absence periode of communist republic government immediate control. At present, in Prince Gong's Mansion, we can no longer see many of the furnishings of those belongings, jewelry, and antiques. We can only see some ancient buildings with traces of scars and unsightly decorations. Under this condition, it can still show the grandeur like a magnificent palace at that time, which shows the special status and great influence of He-Shen (和珅) at that time. There are also distinctions between the main hall and the side halls in the mansion, and the distinction between the vestibule and the rear hall, which once again reflect the noble status of He-Shen (和珅). The building complex is very wide and great, visiting it can be an eye-opener, increase Chinese history knowledge, and benefit us a lot. Entering the exhibition hall, you can see miniatures of the architectural complex, ancient paintings and poems, etc. If you want to appreciate it slowly and in detail, you may not be able to finish your visit within half a day. (050323/x)

Located between the Beihai and Houhai Lakes lies Prince Gong's Mansion, a miniature Forbidden City. The mansion was constructed in 1777 for Heshen, a prominent court official renowned for being the most corrupt official in Chinese history. In 1799, he was accused of corruption and subsequently executed. The mansion was first given to Prince Qing, the 17th and youngest son of the Qianlong Emperor, and in 1851 passed to Prince Gong, the sixth brother of the Xianfeng Emperor and an influential statesman during the Qing Dynasty. In 1921, the neglected mansion came into the hands of the Order of Saint Benedict, who restored it and turned it into a Catholic university until the priests were deported from China in 1951. From the Cultural Revolution onwards, the mansion housed an air conditioning factory, until it was declared a historic site in 1982. Since November 1996, the buildings and the gardens have become a tourist attraction and renovation works were only completed in 2008. 恭王府，位於北京的心臟地帶，是中國現存最大、保存最完整的清代王府建築群。它不僅見證了清朝的輝煌歷史，更是北京城中不可多得的文化瑰寶。遊覽恭王府，彷彿穿越時空，與歷史對話。府內的建築精美絕倫，雕刻細膩，每一磚一瓦都透露著皇家的尊貴與優雅。庭園佈置巧妙，假山流水，曲徑通幽，讓人流連忘返。此外，恭王府內豐富的歷史文物和藝術品展覽，更是讓人大開眼界，成長見識。無論是對歷史有興趣的遊客，或是喜愛庭園建築。
20240922 周日 恭王府，優惠票20r，下午近3點到入口，北京旅游全年皆旺！隨著人潮睇睇清代歷史，到室外就好些，可細看外牆建築特色，有雙魚蝙蝠，應該都是吉祥物。 😰又排乜階呀！唔知是否到“福字碑”摸摸占福氣呢？都4:30pm，五點關門😪，向著出口方向行，都未參觀完就有工作人員催促離開，原來已經五點了。 恭王府地方很大，想細遊就要預多啲時間。

Prince Gong Mansion, tên tiếng Việt là Cung Vương Phủ, hay còn được biết đến với tên gọi nổi tiếng hơn là Phủ Hoà Thân, là dinh thự do đại tham quan thời vua Càn Long là Hoà Thân xây dựng. Phủ nằm tại vị trí đắc địa ở phía Tây Bắc của Cố Cung, từ Tử Cấm Thành bạn có thể đi xe đạp hoặc tàu điện ngầm để đến đây. Có một câu nói nổi tiếng "Một toà Cung Vương phủ, nửa bộ sử Thanh triều", chứng tỏ giá trị lịch sử, kiến trúc và văn hoá to lớn của Cung Vương phủ trong lịch sử Trung Quốc, đặc biệt là nếu bạn muốn tìm hiểu về lịch sử nhà Thanh. Nếu có dịp đến Bắc Kinh, bạn đừng quên ghé thăm toà dinh thự này nhé.
恭王府は清代最大級の王族邸宅で、豪華な建築と精緻な庭園が魅力です。石彫や彩色梁、湖や洞窟が織りなす景観はまるで絵巻物のよう。福の字が刻まれた石碑や西洋風の門、京劇が上演される大戯楼など見どころも豊富。清朝の栄華と文化を体感できる、北京観光の隠れた名所です。
恭王府位於北京西城區，是清代規模最大的一座王府建築羣，為國家5A景區。1780年，和珅奉旨建並住入此府，1851年清廷賜封此宅邸於恭王奕訢，恭王府的名称也因此得来。 恭王府不但十分豪華，還歷經了清朝由鼎盛而至衰亡的歷史進程，承载了极其豐富的歷史文化，故有了「一座恭王府，半部清代史」之説。景區內還有鍍金紀念徽章售賣。

清の時代に乾隆帝の寵臣であった和珅の旧邸宅「恭王府」を訪れてきました。什刹海の西側に位置しており、地下鉄の北海北駅から歩いていくと、すぐに観光客で賑わうエリアに出ました。 歴史の重みと豪華な建築 恭王府は、約2万8000平方メートルもの広大な敷地に、31もの建物が立ち並ぶ大邸宅です。この規模と豪華さから、『紅楼夢』に登場する豪邸、大観園のモデルとも言われているそうです。 私は歴史好きなので、この場所がかつて権力を極めた和珅の邸宅であり、後に清朝の王族に与えられたという背景に非常に興味を惹かれました。特に、和珅が莫大な富を築いたことを示す豪華な建築や、精巧な石彫、彩色梁、そして西洋風の門などは、当時の栄華を物語っているようでした。 庭園と見どころ 恭王府の見どころは、邸宅だけでなく、広大な庭園にもあります。広場や建物内を抜けて庭園に出ると、のんびりと散策を楽しむ人々で賑わっており、私もゆったりとした時間を過ごすことができました。 庭園には池や洞窟が配され、まるで絵巻物のような景色が広がっています。中でも有名なのが、康熙帝直筆の「福」の字が刻まれた石碑です。この福の字を触るとご利益があると言われており、多くの人が列を作っていました。 また、京劇が上演される「大戯楼」も必見です。私は見ることができませんでしたが、清朝時代の文化を感じられる貴重な場所だと感じました。 訪問の感想と注意点 全体的に、恭王府は「中国に来たなぁ」と実感できる、歴史と文化が凝縮された場所だと感じました。ただ、紫禁城や頤和園を見た後だと、少し規模が小さく感じられるかもしれません。 入場料は40元でした。少し高く感じますが、個人的には、歴史的な背景を知ることで十分に楽しめました。 休日はかなり混雑するようなので、事前にチケットを予約するか、平日の訪問をおすすめします。特に、パスポートが必要な場合があるので、忘れないように注意してください。周辺の路地も風情があり、散策するのも楽しいです。

Phủ Hòa Thân, còn được gọi là Cung Vương Phủ, là một công trình kiến trúc lịch sử nổi tiếng tại Bắc Kinh, Trung Quốc. Được xây dựng vào năm 1777 dưới triều đại nhà Thanh, phủ này từng là nơi ở của Hòa Thân, một quan chức quyền lực và giàu có bậc nhất thời bấy giờ. Với diện tích khoảng 60.000 m², Phủ Hòa Thân bao gồm hai khu vực chính: khu nhà ở và khu vườn. Kiến trúc của phủ được thiết kế tinh xảo, thể hiện sự xa hoa với các tòa nhà sơn son thếp vàng, mái ngói lưu ly xanh và những chi tiết chạm khắc tinh tế. Đặc biệt, trong phủ có một sân khấu lớn được xây dựng để Hòa Thân và gia đình thưởng thức nghệ thuật hí kịch, thể hiện niềm đam mê của ông đối với loại hình nghệ thuật này. Ngày nay, Phủ Hòa Thân được bảo tồn gần như nguyên vẹn và mở cửa cho du khách tham quan, trở thành một điểm đến hấp dẫn cho những ai muốn tìm hiểu về lịch sử và kiến trúc thời nhà Thanh

2016年來到北京，最喜歡的景點！精雕細琢的建築，以及和坤在小細節的考究，非常值得一逛！很有意思的一個園林！只可惜遊客實在太多了，有朋友跟我說他在北京讀書的日子，下午來沒多久就將閉館的恭王府逛，倒是十分清幽舒服啊。（ps：來了一定要聽導覽！不然你就會錯過許多有趣好玩的故事跟解說了！）

恭王府位于北京西城区前海西街，是清代规模最大的一座王府，先后作为大贪官和珅、庆亲王永璘的宅邸，后因恭亲王奕訢居住而得名。 恭王府历经了清王朝由鼎盛至衰亡的历史进程，故有“一座恭王府，半部清代史”的说法。恭王府是我国保存最为完整的王府建筑群，拥有各式建筑群落30多处，布局讲究，气派非凡。整体分为府邸和花园两部分，府邸在前（南部），花园在后（北部）。府邸府邸占地约3万平米，由严格的轴线贯穿着的多个四合院组成，分为中、东、西三路建筑，每路各有三个院落。中路：中路最主要的建筑是银安殿和嘉乐堂，殿堂屋顶采用绿琉璃瓦，显示了中路的威严气派，同时也是亲王身份的体现。东路：东路的前院正房是多福轩，和珅的儿子丰绅殷德，后来娶了乾隆皇帝的小女儿固伦和孝公主为妻，就居住于此，使这座豪宅一时成为了实际上的公主府。后进院落正房名为乐道堂，是当年恭亲王奕欣的起居处。西路：西路的院落较为小巧精致，主体建筑为葆光室和锡晋斋。建筑精品当属高大气派的锡晋斋，大厅内有雕饰精美的楠木隔段，是和珅仿紫禁城宁寿宫式样而建。 花园花园位于府邸以北，又名萃锦园，占地28000余平米，有古建筑31处
恭王府周邊交通非常方便，可搭乘公車、地鐵抵達，整個王府保存完整，是規模很大的清朝王府宅邸，最初是清朝官員和珅居住，裡面有關於和珅生平的詳細介紹，也有一些其他的展覽，想像在古代的豪華程度應該媲美頤和園和紫禁城，值得一看，但是假日人潮非常多。

纵所周知，恭王府是大贪官和珅家，注意是和珅，不是王刚哦~强烈推荐去看看，会觉得比故宫要有意思的多，很精致的一座宅子，门票40元/位，一定要蹭个团听听导游介绍，如果光是走走看看会觉得很一般，但是了解了历史和故事，你就会发现绝对不虚此行，也会认识到一个真正的满洲第一美男子和珅别样的魅力，去一次就爱上的地方。无与伦比的藏宝楼，百年前和珅家的复式建筑，福池，天下第一福，观音送子的太湖石，领略下和珅的智慧，万福之地。强烈推荐~ 恭王府，放在这里讲，是因为它素有小故宫之称，是二皇帝和珅故居，后因恭亲王奕昕居住而以恭王府得名。在没去之前对和珅的了解也只是停留在王刚演绎的大贪官层面，但与其府邸一面之缘后，对这位满洲第一美男子的仰慕之情，溢于言表。 和珅家的银安殿，比照故宫建设，以绿琉璃瓦取代故宫的黄琉璃瓦，从外表看并不觉得足够奢华，但细节会让你发现，恭王府邸要比故宫更精致用心。大到和珅家的万福（一座福字碑和9999个廊木上画的蝙蝠），后花园的西洋门（比照圆明园建设），送子观音像（当年从江南花了好几年时间运来，第二年夫人冯氏便为和珅诞下此生唯一的儿子丰绅殷德），福池、摇钱树，独一无二的藏宝楼（和珅以108扇不同形状的窗户辨认里面藏的到底是什么宝贝，至今也只有和珅自己知道的秘密），小到这里的每一个下水道设计成铜钱状（意为流水不流财），所有的床、座椅、书桌全部镶有银饰，时至今日仍熠熠生辉，可见这位满洲男子生活的奢华与特有的用心。
和珅和恭亲王住过的地方，很精致，比故宫有意思，该有的都有，还没有那么多不让进的，门票40，四点半停止入场之后人就少多了，很多房间被改成了展厅放字画之类的展品，东边还有一条小商业街
